description: Pollo en Mole is a culinary masterpiece, showcasing the depth and complexity of Mexican cuisine. Tender chicken is enveloped in a rich, dark mole sauce, a symphony of chiles, spices, nuts, and a hint of chocolate. This traditional dish offers an unforgettable journey through authentic Mexican flavors.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Place chicken pieces in a large pot with 3 cups of chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer until chicken is cooked through, about 20-25 minutes. Remove chicken and set aside. Strain and reserve the broth.

instructions.title: Prepare Chiles and Aromatics
instructions.text: Lightly toast the dried chiles in a dry skillet over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until fragrant, being careful not to burn them. Place toasted chiles in a bowl and cover with hot reserved chicken broth to rehydrate for 15 minutes. Meanwhile, char the tomatoes, onion, and unpeeled garlic cloves in the same dry skillet until softened and lightly browned. Peel the garlic.

instructions.title: Toast Nuts, Seeds, and Spices
instructions.text: In the same skillet, toast almonds, peanuts, sesame seeds, and pumpkin seeds until fragrant and lightly golden. Be careful not to burn them. Separately, lightly toast the cumin, cinnamon, cloves, and anise seeds. Fry the torn corn tortillas in 1 tablespoon of lard or oil until crispy. Set all toasted ingredients aside.

instructions.title: Blend the Mole Base
instructions.text: Drain the rehydrated chiles, reserving the soaking liquid. In a blender, combine the rehydrated chiles, charred tomatoes, onion, garlic, all toasted nuts and seeds, fried tortillas, and toasted spices. Add 1 cup of the reserved chicken broth and blend until a very smooth paste forms. Add more broth as needed to achieve a thick, pourable consistency.

instructions.title: Simmer the Mole Sauce
instructions.text: Heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of lard or oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Carefully pour the blended mole paste into the hot oil. Cook, stirring constantly, for 15-20 minutes until the sauce thickens and darkens, and the raw chile flavor cooks out. This step is crucial for flavor development.

instructions.title: Finish the Mole
instructions.text: Gradually stir in the remaining reserved chicken broth, a little at a time, until the sauce reaches your desired consistency. It should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon. Add the Mexican chocolate tablet and stir until completely dissolved. Season the mole with salt to taste, and a pinch of sugar if desired to balance the flavors. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the mole sauce and simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors and heat through.

instructions.title: Serve and Enjoy
instructions.text: Serve the Pollo en Mole hot, garnished with a sprinkle of sesame seeds. It is traditionally served with Mexican rice and warm corn tortillas for scooping up the delicious sauce. Buen provecho!

tips: For a truly authentic mole, toast your chiles and spices individually until fragrant, being careful not to burn them, as this develops their deep flavor.
If Mexican chocolate is unavailable, use unsweetened dark chocolate (70% cocoa or higher) and add a small pinch of sugar to balance the bitterness.
Mole sauce often tastes even better the next day as the flavors meld. Store leftover mole and chicken separately in the refrigerator for up to 3-4 days.
